t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup. Background split vertically: deep navy on the left, warm limestone on the right. A huge light-weight sans headline runs across both halves, underlined by a thin steel-blue rule. On the navy side, numbered stages in a 3+2 grid with large light numerals, uppercase light titles, short text and a mono document code each, separated by hairline dividers, for <CONTENT>. On the limestone side, an isometric hairline line drawing of a white polypropylene water skid, no shading, with one pipe route highlighted in steel blue. Square corners, no shadows.
signature_idea: A headline that spans a navy/limestone seam ties numbered approval stages to an isometric plant whose one blue route shows the thread through every stage.
strengths: very close to the brand palette and type: light headline, mono codes, one steel-blue accent
doc code per stage makes 'what you approve' concrete
isometric drawing is clean hairline catalogue style, matching the illustration system
split grounds give strong but calm structure
maps easily to a step grid plus illustration component
weaknesses: blue route is decorative and does not map to any stage
headline text crossing the seam half on navy half on limestone hurts legibility
drawing includes generic tanks and gauges, not clearly PP-specific equipment
empty sixth cell in the grid looks unfinished
invented doc codes and accuracy class figures
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone grounds, one steel-blue accent, light sans headline, mono codes, square corners and hairline isometric art are the brand book applied directly.
